title: Chapter 62: Ill Winds 2
content:
Chapter 62

Lan Wangji’s lips trembled faintly, silently forming a name. Up on the rafters, Jiang Cheng nearly shot to his feet.

It was Wei Wuxian!

Yet, aside from that face, nothing about this person resembled the Wei Wuxian they once knew.

The boy they remembered was radiant, impossibly bright, practically vibrating with effortless charm and a grin that never left his face—someone who couldn't be bothered to walk in a straight line if his life depended on it. But this figure stepped out of the shadows draped in a bone-chilling, suffocating gloom. He was striking, yes, but deathly pale, and the curve of his lips carried nothing but sheer malice.

The shock was paralyzing. With the situation entirely murky, neither of the eavesdroppers on the roof dared make a reckless move. Shaken to their cores, they simply pressed themselves flatter against the eaves, peering through the cracks between the tiles.

Down in the room, the black-robed youth turned around with deliberate slowness. Wen Chao was still frantically shielding his face, his voice reduced to a dry, wheezing gasp: "Wen Zhuliu... Wen Zhuliu!"

Hearing the pathetic whimper, Wei Wuxian’s eyes crinkled, and his lips curled into a lazy smirk. "Even now, you honestly think calling his name is going to save you?"

He took a few languid strides forward, his boot nudging against something pale on the floorboards. Glancing down, he saw the meat bun Wen Chao had hurled away moments earlier.

Wei Wuxian arched a brow. "What’s the matter? Picky eater?"

Wen Chao collapsed off his stool, thrashing on the floor in a frantic, unhinged wail: "I won't eat it! I won't! I won't eat it!"

Howling like a wounded dog, he dragged his fingerless stumps across the timber. The trailing hem of his heavy traveling cloak slid away from his waist, exposing his legs. They dangled beneath him like useless, decorative appendages—heavily bandaged and unnervingly skeletal. His frantic thrashing pulled the wrappings loose, revealing gaps where strips of gauze peeled back to expose stark, glistening bone clingy with raw shreds of red sinew.

The meat on his legs had been methodically carved away, piece by agonizing piece. And worst of all... he had likely been forced to swallow every single bite himself.

Wen Chao’s shrill, bloodcurdling shrieks bounced off the hollow walls of the outpost. Wei Wuxian acted completely deaf to the noise, flipping his robes back with effortless grace as he took a seat at a neighboring table.

A second oil lamp flared to life with a sullen pop. Bathed in the flickering yellow glow, half of Wei Wuxian’s face sat in the light, the other half swallowed by pitch-black shadow. He let his arm dangle off the edge of the table. From the darkness beneath the wood, an ashen, bloodless little face slowly drifted into view. A sickening, rhythmic crunching sound began to echo from the gloom.

A pale child was crouched at his feet like a ravenous little animal, gnawing eagerly on whatever scraps Wei Wuxian had just tossed down.

Wei Wuxian withdrew his hand, giving the ghastly ghost-child’s head two gentle, affectionate pats over its patchy, thinning hair. Clamping its prize between its teeth, the creature swiveled around to sit against his boots. It wrapped its tiny arms around Wei Wuxian’s shin, chewing viciously while fixing Wen Zhuliu with a cold, glittering glare.

Between its gnashing teeth were two severed human fingers.

Needless to say, they belonged to Wen Chao.

Up on the roof, Lan Wangji’s knuckles whitened as his grip clamped hard aroundBichen’s hilt, staring intently at the macabre spirit and the equally chilling young man controlling it.

Wen Zhuliu stood his ground, shielding Wen Chao with his body. Wei Wuxian kept his chin dipped, his expression veiled in the dark. "Wen Zhuliu, do you really believe you have what it takes to keep this dog breathing under my watch?"

Wen Zhuliu answered flatly, "I will die trying."

Wei Wuxian let out a sharp, mocking scoff. "What a loyal, devoted Wen dog."

"A debt of gratitude must be repaid."

Wei Wuxian’s demeanor snapped into pure venom, his voice cracking like a whip: "A debt of gratitude?! What a sick joke! Why the hell shouldyourdebt of gratitude be paid with other people's lives?!"

Before the roar faded, a ragged scream tore from Wen Chao behind him. The wretch had scrambled into a corner, throwing all his weight against the wooden planks as if he could somehow squeeze through the hairline cracks in the wall. Without warning, a crimson blur dropped from the rafters with a heavy smack, slamming squarely onto his back. A woman in brilliant scarlet robes, her face a bruised, mottled iron-blue beneath tangled black hair, pinned him down. The violent contrast of her garish silk, sickly skin, and dark locks was nauseating. Her claw-like fingers dug into the bandages wrapped around Wen Chao’s head—and yanked with brutal force!

Wen Zhuliu had only just finished dressing the burns; the fresh salve, charred flesh, and linen were fused into a sticky mess. Skin cooked by fire was extraordinarily fragile to begin with. That savage tear ripped away the unpeeled scabs and gossamer-thin layers of regenerating flesh in one clean sweep, tearing his lips clean off in the process. In the span of a single heartbeat, the lumpy, bald skull transformed into a dripping, unrecognizable dome of raw meat.

Wen Chao passed out cold on the spot.

The second the scream broke, Wen Zhuliu whipped around to save him. Up on the roof, Lan Wangji and Jiang Cheng tightened their grip, poised to strike. But before anyone could move, a shrill screech ripped through the room as the ghost-child at Wei Wuxian’s feet pounced. Wen Zhuliu drove a palm strike forward, landing squarely on the child's brow, only for a searing pain to bite into his hand—the creature had sunk its jagged teeth deep into his flesh. Unable to shake it off, Wen Zhuliu ignored the pain and lunged toward Wen Chao anyway. The ghost-child clamped down, tore away a thick mouthful of muscle, spat it out, and immediately began chewing its way down the man's palm.

Wen Zhuliu caught the child's skull with his left hand, muscles coiling to crush the tiny, freezing head bare-handed. But the woman in scarlet tossed the bloody bandages aside and dropped to all fours, skittering across the floorboards like an insect. With a vicious swipe of her hands, ten bloody gouges opened across his flesh. Swarmed by two feral entities tearing at him from both sides, Wen Zhuliu couldn't guard his front and back at once, instantly thrown into messy disarray. Glancing sideways, he caught sight of Wei Wuxian watching the carnage with a leisurely, mocking smirk—and lunged straight for him.

Up on the roof, both men snapped to attention. Lan Wangji struck downward with a concussive palm strike, shattering the tiles as the roof caved in. Dropping through the ceiling onto the second floor, he landed squarely between Wen Zhuliu and Wei Wuxian. Wen Zhuliu faltered in shock, and in that exact split-second, a streak of crackling purple lightning tore through the air.Zidianwhipped around his throat, coiling tight three times with an electric hiss before violently hauling upward!

Wen Zhuliu’s towering, muscular frame was hoisted into the air by the whip, dangling off the floor as a sickening, wet crunch of snapping cervical vertebrae cracked through the room.

At the same moment, Wei Wuxian’s pupils contracted. Snatching the black flute from his sash, he spun on his heel and sprang upright. The ghost-child and the blue-faced woman instantly broke off their attack, retreating to his flank, baring their teeth and hissing warily at the two intruders.

Behind them, Wen Zhuliu wasn't dead just yet. His face was swollen a suffocating, violent crimson, limbs jerking in spastic convulsions, his eyes bulging so hard they looked ready to pop from their sockets. The ghost-child snarled at Lan Wangji and Jiang Cheng, dripping with pure hostility. Wei Wuxian raised a casual hand, signaling it to stand down, his eyes flicking back and forth between the two men standing before him.

Three people, yet not a single soul broke the silence.

After an eternity, Jiang Cheng’s arm swung forward, tossing something across the gap.

Wei Wuxian caught it on reflex.

"Your sword!" Jiang Cheng barked.

Wei Wuxian’s hand slowly drifted down. He stared at the scabbard ofSuibian, hesitating for a long beat before murmuring, "...Thanks."

Another heavy hush hung over them. Then, Jiang Cheng closed the distance, throwing a heavy slap against Wei Wuxian's shoulder. "You little bastard! Where the hell have you been these past three months?!"

The words were an abrasive curse, but the tone beneath was pure, unadulterated ecstasy. Lan Wangji didn't move an inch, his eyes locked unblinkingly onto Wei Wuxian.

Stunned by the blow, Wei Wuxian blinked, then broke out into a laugh, clapping Jiang Cheng's shoulder right back. "Haha! It’s a long story, truly a long story!"

Those two hearty claps seemed to dispel a fraction of the icy, suffocating aura clinging to him. Torn between burning rage and overwhelming relief, Jiang Cheng pulled him into a crushing embrace, only to shove him back just as violently, roaring, "Didn't we agree to meet at that crummy town at the foot of the mountain?! I waited five whole days and didn't see a single hair on your head! If you're going to get yourself killed, at least do it in front of me! These past three months have been a complete nightmare!"

Wei Wuxian flipped his robes and slumped back onto the edge of the table, waving a dismissive hand. "I told you, it's a long story. A pack of Wen dogs was turning the whole place upside down hunting for me back then. They ambushed me right at the post, dragged me off, and tossed me into some hellhole to rot."

As he spoke, the blue-faced woman crawled over on all fours. The demonic ferocity she’d displayed while tearing flesh earlier vanished; resting her bruised chin against Wei Wuxian’s thigh, she looked for all the world like a pampered concubine purring for her master's affection, letting out soft, clicking giggles. Wei Wuxian leaned casually against the table, his right hand idly stroking the sleek length of her hair.

Lan Wangji’s expression grew progressively colder, his jaw set like stone.

The sight turned Jiang Cheng’s stomach, but bewilderment quickly overtook his disgust. "What hellhole? I interrogated every single soul in that town, and they all swore they'd never seen you!"

"You asked the locals?" Wei Wuxian scoffed. "A bunch of backwater peasants terrified of trouble? Who'd have the guts to tell you the truth? Besides, the Wen dogs definitely threatened to slit their throats if they talked. Of course they played dumb."

Jiang Cheng spat, "Cowardly bastards!" He pressed on, "Where did they take you? Qishan? Nightless City? How did you break out? And how did you end up like this... What the hell are these two things? They actually take orders from you?! Lan-er-gongzi and I took the mission to track down and execute Wen Chao and Wen Zhuliu tonight, only to find someone had beat us to it. I never dreamed it was you! Did you alter those talismans, too?"

Catching Lan Wangji’s unyielding stare out of the corner of his eye, Wei Wuxian flashed an easy, teasing grin. "Pretty much. If I told you I stumbled into a hidden cave, found ancient secret manuals left behind by an immortal master, mastered them, and came out to slaughter everyone in sight... would you believe me?"

Jiang Cheng scoffed, "Wake up, you've been reading too many cheap adventure novels. As if the world is crawling with hidden grottos and peerless scriptures!"

Wei Wuxian held out his hands with an exaggerated sigh. "See? You ask, but when I tell you, you call me a liar. We'll catch up on the details when we have time."

Jiang Cheng glanced sideways at Lan Wangji, realizing this wasn't the kind of secret you spilled in front of an outsider from another clan. Pulling back his smile, he nodded. "Fine. We'll talk later. Just... good to have you back."

Wei Wuxian’s eyes softened. "Yeah. Good to be back."

Jiang Cheng muttered the words under his breath a few times, then abruptly delivered another hard smack to his arm. "You really are something... Falling into the hands of those Wen dogs and actually crawling out alive!"

Wei Wuxian smirked, puffing his chest slightly. "Naturally. Who do you think I am?"

"Wipe that smug look off your face!" Jiang Cheng snapped. "If you were alive, you should've dragged your ass back sooner!"

"I literally just got out!" Wei Wuxian argued. "The second I heard you and Shijie were safe, that you were rebuilding the Jiang Clan and marshaling forces for the war, I figured I'd drop a few Wen dogs on the way to lighten your load. You've had a rough three months."

Hearing that, the memory of the grueling, sleepless nights spent dragging their shattered clan from the brink flickered across Jiang Cheng’s face. He cleared his throat, masking his vulnerability with his usual prickly bark: "Take this damn sword of yours! I've been waiting for you to come back so I can stop hauling two blades around like an idiot, getting pestered with questions everywhere I go!"

"Wei Ying."

Lan Wangji’s voice cut through the air, cool and sharp.

Having stood in stony silence the entire time, his sudden interruption made both Jiang Cheng and Wei Wuxian turn his way. As if only just remembering his presence, Wei Wuxian tilted his head with a polite, distant nod. "Hanguang-jun."

Lan Wangji asked, "Were you the one who slaughtered the Wen disciples along the road?"

"Naturally."

Jiang Cheng chimed in, "Knew it was you. Why kill them one by one, though? Seems like a massive waste of effort."

"Because it's fun," Wei Wuxian replied smoothly, a dark undertone lacing his words. "Playing them to death. Wiping them out all at once is letting them off too easy. I want them to watch their people drop one by one, carving them up slow. Wen Chao goes without saying—I haven't had half my fun with him yet. As for Wen Zhuliu... he took Wen Ruohan's favor, abandoned his own name to join the Wen dogs, all to guard this spoiled bastard." A chilling sneer broke across his lips. "He wants to protect him? Then I’m going to make him watch Wen Chao rot right under his nose, inch by inch, until he's neither man nor ghost."

The smile on his face was three parts icy, three parts sadistic, and three parts genuine, sickening delight.

Lan Wangji took in every twitch of that expression, taking a single step forward. "What method are you using to control these dark entities?"

The smirk on Wei Wuxian’s lips vanished, his eyes narrowing into a cold slit.

Jiang Cheng picked up on the hostility immediately. "Lan-er-gongzi, what are you trying to say?"

Lan Wangji kept his gaze locked on Wei Wuxian. "Answer me."

The ghost-child and the woman hissed, stirring with restless agitation. Wei Wuxian cast a single sideways glance at them, and they reluctantly backed down, melting into the shadows. Turning back to Lan Wangji, he arched a brow. "And if... I choose not to answer?"

In the blink of an eye, Wei Wuxian twisted his torso, effortlessly slipping past Lan Wangji’s sudden, lightning-fast grab. Stepping back three paces, he said, "Lan Zhan, we just reunited after all this time, and you're already throwing hands? A bit harsh, don't you think?"

Lan Wangji didn't waste breath on words, striking again. Wei Wuxian parried and deflected with blinding speed. Slapping his wrist away for the third time, Wei Wuxian scoffed, "Here I thought we were at least acquaintances. Escalating to violence over a difference of opinion... aren't you being a little heartless?"

"Answer!"

Jiang Cheng stepped directly between them. "Lan-er-gongzi!"

Wei Wuxian chimed in from behind him, "Lan-er-gongzi, what you're asking isn't something I can sum up in two words. Besides, it's a bizarre question. If I started interrogating you about the secret arts of the Gusu Lan Clan, would you give me an honest breakdown?"

Lan Wangji sidestepped Jiang Cheng, reaching straight for him again. Wei Wuxian brought the flute horizontal, barring his path. "Crossing the line now, aren't we? Why so unyielding? Lan Zhan, what the hell do you actually want?"

Lan Wangji ground out every syllable: "Come back to Gusu with me."

Both Wei Wuxian and Jiang Cheng froze.

A second later, Wei Wuxian burst into laughter. "Go back to Gusu with you? The Cloud Recesses? What on earth would I do there?"

Then, understanding dawned on his face with mock amusement. "Ah. Right. I forgot—your uncle, Lan Qiren, despises crooked heretics like me the most. And you're his prized pupil, so naturally you'd feel the same. Haha. I refuse."

Jiang Cheng’s guard flared, glaring at Lan Wangji. "Lan-er-gongzi, we all respect the principles of the Lan Clan. But Wei Wuxian saved your life in the cave of the Xuanwu of Slaughter, and you two bled together. To turn around and demand to drag him in for judgment the second you lay eyes on him... aren't you being a little too cold-blooded?"

Wei Wuxian glanced at him, impressed. "Look at you! Talking like a real clan leader."

"Shut up," Jiang Cheng snapped.

Lan Wangji said, "I do not seek to condemn him."

"Then why demand he return to Gusu with you?" Jiang Cheng pressed. "Lan-er-gongzi, with the war raging, your clan should be focusing on slaughtering Wen dogs. Why are you clinging to your rigid dogmas at a time like this?"

Outnumbered two to one, Lan Wangji didn't yield an inch, his eyes fixed unswervingly on Wei Wuxian. "Wei Ying. Walking the dark path carries a price. History has proven there are no exceptions."

Wei Wuxian’s tone was flat. "I can afford it."

Seeing his utter nonchalance, Lan Wangji’s voice dropped into a heavy rumble: "This path damages the body, and it erodes the mind."

"Whether it damages my body, and how much, is something I know better than anyone," Wei Wuxian countered. "As for my mind—my heart is my own. I know what I'm doing."

"There are forces beyond your control."

A flicker of irritation crossed Wei Wuxian’s brow. "I have it under control."

Lan Wangji took another step forward, opening his mouth to speak, but Wei Wuxian’s eyes narrowed into dangerous slits. "At the end of the day, what do outsiders know about my mind? And what business is it of theirs anyway?"

Lan Wangji went rigid, hurt flashing through his eyes before flaring into sudden, uncharacteristic fury: "...Wei Wuxian!"

Wei Wuxian snapped right back: "Lan Wangji! Must you pick a fight with me right now?! You want me to go to the Cloud Recesses so your clan can lock me up?! Who do you think you are, and who the hell does the Gusu Lan Clan think they are?! Do you honestly think I won't fight back?!"

The air between them crackled with raw, volatile hostility. Lan Wangji’s knuckles turned bone-white over the hilt of his sword.

Jiang Cheng cut in with a venomous sneer, "Lan-er-gongzi, the Wen menace is far from broken, and every clan needs all the firepower they can get. Everyone is struggling just to survive; why is Gusu Lan stretching its hands into our business? Wei Wuxian fights for our side—are you trying to discipline our allies?"

Wei Wuxian’s expression smoothed over into an easy shrug. "Exactly. As long as the dead are Wen dogs, why do you care how I kill them?"

The two had grown up bouncing off each other’s rhythms; their seamless front left no openings. Jiang Cheng drove the stake home: "Pardon my bluntness, but even if someone had the right to interrogate him, Wei Wuxian isn't a disciple of your house. Gusu Lan has zero jurisdiction here. No matter who he leaves with, he isn't going anywhere with you."

Hearing that, Lan Wangji froze. He looked up at Wei Wuxian, his throat bobbing as he managed a single, choked rasp: "I..."

Before he could finish, a faint, agonized whimper broke from the corner. The spell shattered, and Wei Wuxian and Jiang Cheng’s attention snapped away. Bypassing Lan Wangji without another glance, they strode toward Wen Zhuliu and Wen Chao.

Wen Zhuliu was still dangling fromZidian, convulsing in silent agony. Slumped on the floor half-dead, Wen Chao slowly peeled his eyelids open, only to be met by two young faces looking down at him from above.

Two faces, equally young, equally familiar. Both had once worn expressions of absolute despair, excruciating agony, and bone-deep hatred before him. And now, looking down on him like an insect, their expressions were mirrored—wearing the exact same icy sneer, eyes glittering with murderous malice.

Wen Chao didn't scream anymore, nor did he try to crawl away. He simply stared blankly, cradling his fingerless stumps against his chest as drool spilled from the ruined mess of his mouth. Wei Wuxian delivered a sharp kick, forcing him into a kowtow facing the direction of Yunmeng. The raw bone and torn meat grinding against the floorboards pulled a series of wretched shrieks from his throat, echoing terribly in the empty room.

Jiang Cheng frowned. "Why is his voice so shrill?"

Wei Wuxian said, "Missing a certain part of his anatomy—naturally it pitches up."

Disgust washed over Jiang Cheng's face. "You cut it off?"

"Give me some credit, that's disgusting," Wei Wuxian scoffed. "That darling concubine of his lost her mind and bit it off."

Behind them, Lan Wangji still stood motionless, his eyes locked on the scene.

Remembering his presence, Wei Wuxian turned around with an easy, pleasant smile. "Lan-er-gongzi, what comes next probably isn't suited for your delicate eyes. Why don't you see yourself out?"

Though phrased as a polite request, the tone brooked zero negotiation.

Jiang Cheng added, cold and distant, "Indeed. Lan-er-gongzi, Wen Chao and Wen Zhuliu have fallen into our hands; our mission is complete, and our paths diverge here. What remains is personal family vengeance. Please, take your leave."

Lan Wangji’s gaze remained glued to Wei Wuxian. But Wei Wuxian’s attention had already been reclaimed by his dying prey. Looking down at Wen Chao and Wen Zhuliu, his eyes sparkled with a manic, cruel ecstasy. Jiang Cheng wore the exact same feral expression. Drowning in the intoxicating high of absolute vengeance, neither had an ounce of patience left to entertain an outsider.

After an agonizing silence, Lan Wangji turned and descended the stairs.

He stepped out of the relay station and stood near the threshold for a long time, yet his boots refused to carry him away.

Time blurred until a bloodcurdling, protracted howl of agony ripped through the dead of night.

Lan Wangji tilted his head up, his pristine white robes and forehead ribbon snapping violently in the biting wind.

The night was finally breaking; the sun in the sky was about to rise.

And the sun on earth was crashing down into dust.
